**- What I did**

Improve performance of function `daemon.Containers()` (used by `docker ps`) to mitigate a latency increase when running large number of containers using the containerd image store. See #47581 for more info.

fixes #47581

**- How I did it**

Refactored function `daemon.Containers()` to collect info for containers concurrently, rather than sequentially. This improves the performance from O(N) to O(log2(N)). See the commits for a more detailed description.

**- How to verify it**

To verify correctness, I added a unit test in `daemon/list_test.go` that starts a random number of containers (from 0 to 256) and then verifies that `daemon.Containers()` returns a correct listing of them. I ran the test multiple times without failure.

I also added a similar integration test in `integration/container/list_test.go` and verified the test passes.

Finally, to verify the performance improvement, I manually configured the docker engine with the containerd image store (by adding `"features": {"containerd-snapshotter": true}` in `/etc/docker/daemon.json`), then started a large number of containers (e.g., 100), and then did `time docker ps`. I verified that with this change, `docker ps` executes in O(log2(N)), where N is the number of containers, compared to O(N) prior to this change.

@thaJeztah: I noticed the following integration test fails with this PR:

```
=== Failed
=== FAIL: amd64.integration-cli TestDockerCLIPsSuite/TestPsListContainersBase (1.10s)
    docker_cli_ps_test.go:56: assertion failed: false (bool) != true (true bool): ALL: Container list is not in the correct order: 
```

It seems it's expecting `docker ps` to list containers in a certain order, which this PR doesn't guarantee given that is runs concurrent threads to gather the container listing, so the order of the results is not guaranteed.

I don't believe `docker ps` has any ordering guarantees, so I am thinking the failing integration test is overly strict and needs changing. Am I correct?

> I don't believe docker ps has any ordering guarantees, so I am thinking the failing integration test is overly strict and needs changing. Am I correct?

Oh! Yes, order _does_ matter; and I :see_no_evil: was actually looking at that when I was reviewing, then forgot (for the tests, I was wondering why we only checked the length, and not a `DeepEqual`, which likely should work with no filters applied)


containers must be listed in descending order (last created container must appear first in the list). This order allows for various uses, and it's not unlikely that users depend on things like;

View the last X containers;

```bash
docker ps -a | head -n 3
CONTAINER ID   IMAGE           COMMAND                  CREATED             STATUS                      PORTS     NAMES
c1a80713617b   nginx:alpine    "/docker-entrypoint.…"   About an hour ago   Up About an hour            80/tcp    pensive_murdock
c6de2c72b5ae   docker-dev      "hack/dind bash"         19 hours ago        Up 19 hours                           stoic_driscoll
```

Or getting the ID of the last container;

```bash
docker ps -q | head -n 1
c1a80713617b
```

So the `filterByNameIDMatches` method is currently responsible for ordering, but the method is un-exported, and not documented, so doesn't clearly define that contract;
https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/63ea5dc10e99e070a00c449e7fd78916a9fd125a/daemon/list.go#L169
https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/63ea5dc10e99e070a00c449e7fd78916a9fd125a/daemon/list.go#L219-L221

:point_up: honestly, I think we should move that sorting out of the `filterByNameIDMatches` function to put it more in plain sight, and add a clear comment stating that containers MUST be sorted before we reach the loop calling `includeContainerInList`, because that function depends on containers being sorted for some filters (like `before=<some container>`, `since=<some container>`) https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/63ea5dc10e99e070a00c449e7fd78916a9fd125a/daemon/list.go#L126C10-L126C32


So, yeah, looks like (unfortunately) we need to add a sort at the end of the list function as well. A possible alternative is to update containers "in place", e.g. something like;

```go
resultsMut.Lock()
results[i] = newC
resultsMut.Unlock()
```

issue_context.body: ### Description When using containerd as the image store, `docker ps` has to query containerd for every container. Notably, it seems to do this for every single container in the system, not just running ones (which is what `docker ps` shows by default). ### Reproduce 1. Run a few containers (the more, the slower it gets) 2. Run `docker ps` ### Expected behavior `docker ps` should be a fast operation. I'm haven't looked at what dockerd is reading from containerd yet, though it is hitting ` containerd.services.content.v1.Content/Info` Some of the issue is these reads are happening sequentially, so it just takes time to build up the result. Did a quick profiling and yes, `docker ps` with the containerd image store is slower than without it.

Average `docker ps` latency with 50 running containers on a Linux Ubuntu host with 16 CPU cores and 32GB RAM:

```
With Docker Image Store: 0.018 secs.
With Containerd Image Store: 0.25 secs
```

Thus `docker ps` is ~14x slower when using the containerd image store when running 50 containers.

Furthermore, the `docker ps` latency with the containerd image store scales linearly with the number of containers, where as it remains fairly constant with the Docker image store.

I'll take a look to see how we can improve it.

Here's a PR that improves performance of `docker ps` by parallelizing the way it collects container info from the underlying image store: https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/49365.

It reduces the latency from O(N) to O(log2(N)), which helps a bit when running large number of containers, particularly with the containerd image store.
